beats.say: Patrick Stewart went from unknown British Shakespearean actor to global star.
Born in Mirfield in Yorkshire, he joined the prestigious Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966.
When he joined Star Trek: The Next Generation, he told the cast they were not there to have fun.

shots.src: commons-search:Star Trek The Next Generation set

beats.say: Yet portraying Captain Picard brought him international stardom, and Queen Elizabeth II knighted him for drama in 2010.
He proved theatrical discipline could conquer global sci-fi television forever.
Which Captain Picard moment is your favourite?

facts: When Stewart was picked for the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation, the Los Angeles Times called him an unknown British Shakespearean actor.
Sir Patrick Stewart was born on 13 July 1940 in Mirfield in the West Riding of Yorkshire.
Stewart became a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966.
Early on Patrick told us all that we weren’t there to have fun.
He gained international stardom for his portrayal of Captain Jean-Luc Picard in the sci-fi series Star Trek: The Next Generation.
He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II for his services to drama in 2010.
